manuscripts.title: Weighted Dilation Graphs, Smooth Shifted Primes and Totient Fibers
claims: For all epsilon>0, infinitely many n have totient-fiber cardinality g(n)>n^(1-epsilon).
For each fixed 0<delta<1/4, number of primes 2x<p<=5x with largest prime factor P+(p-1)<=x^delta is >=x^(1-o(1)); not a positive limiting proportion.

manuscripts.title: Poisson–Dirichlet Law for Prime Predecessors
claims: For each fixed k and bounded continuous F, ordinary prime-averaged distribution of k largest logarithmically normalized prime factors (with multiplicity) of p-1 tends to Poisson–Dirichlet PD(1).
Statement implies stronger fixed-u Dickman smoothness asymptotic, not simply the subpower-count lower bound of the companion.

manuscripts.title: Prime Predecessors with an Even Number of Prime Factors
claims: Infinitely many prime p with p-1 squarefree and Omega(p-1) even, equivalently Möbius mu(p-1)=1.
Parity assertion requires distinct signed-correlation work, not implied merely by predecessor smoothness.
